newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan puts up seven power plants for tender.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan puts up seven power plants for tender.

text.p: Kazakhstan announced on Thursday international tenders for the right to manage seven power stations in the east region of the former Soviet republic.

Mirkhat Nigmatullin, spokesman at the Finance Ministry's privatisation department, said the government was offering investors the right to manage seven power stations, grouped into four separate tender projects, over 20 years.
The first project groups the AO Shulbinskaya hydroelectric station, in the town of Shulba, with two thermal power stations in the town of Semipalatinsk.
The second groups the AO Ustkamenogorskaya hydroelectric station and AO Ustkamenogorskaya thermal power station in the town of Ust Kamenogorsk.
The Sogrinskaya and Leninogorskaya thermal power stations are the facilities on offer in the third and the fourth tenders.
The spokesman gave no details on capacities at the stations, the amount of investment needed or terms of the tenders. He said bids would be accepted until April 30 inclusive.
Nigmatullin said investors must present clear programmes on ensuring energy efficiency, stable salaries for employees and adequate investment to boost the capacities.
The winners must also pay a bonus to Kazakhstan's budget.
The sale is part of Kazakhstan's wide privatisation programme, in which most of the energy-rich Central Asian state's oil, gas and electricity infrastructure are being sold off to foreign investors.
